question.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of OTC (Over-the-Counter) derivative contracts?

answer.text: They are customized contracts with counterparty credit risk
They are standardized contracts guaranteed by a clearing corporation
They require daily mark-to-market margin payments
They can only be settled through physical delivery

explanation.text: The Logic: OTC derivatives are customized, bilaterally negotiated contracts that carry decentralized counterparty credit risk because there is no exchange or clearing-corporation intermediary. The Trap: Standardization, clearing-corporation guarantee and daily mark-to-market margining are features of exchange-traded derivatives, not OTC; both OTC and exchange-traded contracts can settle in cash or by physical delivery. Note: Per the workbook, OTC has no formal centralized limits on positions, leverage or margining; this is different from saying OTC has "no margins" altogether.
